lesson_title: Debit and Credit Are Just Left and Right
hook_text: Debit does not mean minus and credit does not mean plus. Here is what they really mean.
clip_script: Debit means left. Credit means right. That is it. Now write the accounting equation across the page: assets on the left, owner's equity and liabilities on the right. Assets live on the left, so they grow on the left: debit. Owner's equity and liabilities live on the right, so they grow on the right: credit. Income makes the owner richer, so it grows on the right too. Expenses and drawings make the owner poorer, so they grow on the left. Two families. Debit family: assets, expenses, drawings. Credit family: liabilities, capital, income. Want to make an account smaller? Write on the other side. Paying money out credits bank. And every transaction has one debit and one credit of the same amount. That is why, at the end of the month, the two sides of the whole ledger must agree.
visual_style: The equation A = OE + L stretched across a page; account cards slide to the left or right to join two coloured families; a T-account with Dr and Cr labels.
pacing: A crisp opening myth-buster, steady family sorting, a firm final rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort fourteen real accounts into their families.
